Nicholas Sofroniew
Jack Lindsey

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: In this paper, we provide evidence that LLMs do possess such workspace-like representations.

span.label: global workspace / conscious-access-like representations in large language models
span.quote: Specifically, we observe that language models maintain a privileged set of internal representations, available for report, modulation, and flexible internal reasoning, atop a much larger volume of automatic processing.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: The Jacobian lens is a technique for inspecting the contents of the residual stream at these intermediate layers.

span.label: The lens is acknowledged as an approximate and incomplete proxy for whatever the model's real workspace is.
span.quote: The Jacobian lens is an imperfect tool, which we believe only approximately and incompletely captures the model’s underlying workspace structure.

span.label: It can only name concepts that happen to be single tokens in the vocabulary.
span.quote: This construction means that the set of concepts the lens can name is exactly the set of concepts that have a single-token name in the tokenizer's vocabulary.

span.label: The readout is a flat bag of concepts and cannot show how they are bound or structured together.
span.quote: Even setting the vocabulary issue aside, the J-lens treats the workspace as a flat collection of independently active concept vectors.

span.label: Readouts are not always interpretable, and the rate of uninterpretable ones was not characterised systematically.
span.quote: In our experience this is the typical case at workspace-layer positions, but it is not the universal one: at some positions and layers, the top lens tokens are ones we cannot make sense of.

span.label: The apparent emptiness of the early layers may be a fact about the model or an artefact of the lens; the authors cannot tell which.
span.quote: W e do not know whether this is a fact about the model or an artifact of the lens.

span.label: No mechanism is offered for how a representation comes to enter the workspace.
span.quote: W e have not characterized what causes a representation to enter it.

span.label: The authors decline to claim the J-space is sufficient for alignment monitoring, since automatic or well-practised misaligned behaviour could bypass it.
span.quote: W e do not feel comfortable making the stronger claim that monitoring the J-space is sufficient for alignment monitoring, or that any sophisticated plan the model might execute must be represented there.

span.label: Findings are from large production models only; scaling and training-time emergence are untested.
span.quote: W e have studied the workspace primarily in fully trained production LLMs of considerable size.

span.label: The analogy to global workspace theory is explicitly partial: architectural features such as encapsulated processors and recurrent broadcast are not claimed.
span.quote: Despite these similarities, we do not claim that language models reproduce the full architecture global workspace theory ascribes to the brain

span.label: a positive control on the ablation itself, checking it removes the content the J-space was shown to carry
span.quote: W e first verify, as a positive control, that the ablation removes the kind of content the preceding sections showed the J-space to carry.

span.label: a story-writing task run under the same ablation, scoring general story quality alongside the rate of experiential language
span.quote: A story-writing control confirms the effect is not due to broad degradation of writing capability: ablation only slightly reduces graded story quality, while still reducing the rate of experiential language within those stories ( §A.23 ).

span.label: zeroing equal-sized, layer-matched sets of randomly chosen heads - the sentence states the control and not its outcome, so no outcome is recorded here
span.quote: W e zero the heads' outputs at every token position, and as a control we do the same to equal-sized, layer-matched sets of randomly chosen heads.

span.label: a perturbation of equal magnitude applied to a different concept of the same category
span.quote: As a control, to ensure the effect on avoidance behavior is not simply due to perturbations generically degrading the model’s capabilities, or due to noise leading to regression-to-mean effects, we tried applying a perturbation of equal magnitude, inhibiting the J-lens vector of some other concept of the same category as the primed one.

span.label: global workspace - the theory's sense: a shared space a representation is posted to, from which many downstream processes can read
span.quote: A representation becomes consciously accessible when it is posted to a shared "global workspace" from which many downstream processes can read .

span.label: global workspace - a processing hub that integrates and broadcasts, so the information can be used for flexible internal reasoning and report
span.quote: Under the theory, the workspace is a processing hub that integrates and broadcasts information, allowing it to be used for flexible internal reasoning and report .

span.label: nameable concept - bounded by the tokenizer: exactly those concepts holding a single-token name, which is what the lens can report at all
span.quote: This construction means that the set of concepts the lens can name is exactly the set of concepts that have a single-token name in the tokenizer's vocabulary.

span.label: global workspace - what the paper explicitly does NOT claim language models reproduce
span.quote: we do not claim that language models reproduce the full architecture global workspace theory ascribes to the brain

span.label: extends → the logit lens
span.quote: While the logit lens assumes that representations use the same coordinates in all layers, the Jacobian lens corrects for representational changes that take place across layers, allowing it to uncover meaningful information in earlier layers where the logit lens produces uninterpretable readouts.

span.label: builds-on → Hernandez et al., per-relation linear maps from Jacobians
span.quote: The J-lens applies the same first-order approximation to the map from activations to model outputs, rather than to a single relation.

span.label: replicates → Li et al., logit-lens decoding and patching of multi-hop intermediates
span.quote: Closest to our approach, Li et al. use the logit lens to decode the intermediate entity in a multi-hop query from middle layers and patch along the decoded directions to redirect the answer, paralleling the internal-reasoning results of §3.3 .

span.label: builds-on → work on implicit chain-of-thought
span.quote: More closely related to our method is work on “implicit chain-of-thought” , which establishes that training on auxiliary reasoning text can shape computation in that context, even when the auxiliary text is dropped at inference.

span.label: consciously accessible information —operationalised-as→ global workspace
span.quote: A representation becomes consciously accessible when it is posted to a shared "global workspace" from which many downstream processes can read .

span.label: LLMs maintain a privileged set of internal representations available for report, modulation, and flexible reasoning
span.quote: language models maintain a privileged set of internal representations, available for report, modulation, and flexible internal reasoning

span.label: an analogous accessible/unconscious functional distinction has emerged in modern AI models
span.quote: an analogous functional distinction has emerged in modern AI

span.label: a new interpretability technique surfaces the concepts a model is poised to verbalize
span.quote: a new interpretability technique, which surfaces the concepts a model is poised

span.label: verbalizable vs automatic internal representations
span.quote: the concepts a model is poised

span.label: global workspace (LLM analog)
span.quote: a privileged set of internal representations, available for report, modulation, and flexible internal reasoning
